Sequential Lumipulse testing reduced the p-tau217 indeterminate zone

In 562 consecutive memory-clinic patients, using the p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio only after an intermediate p-tau217 result reduced indeterminate classifications from 17.8% to 12.3% and was estimated to spare 56 confirmatory CSF or amyloid-PET tests per 1,000 patients.

Key quantitative results: Core 1 amyloid positivity was 71.2% (400/562); p-tau217 AUC was 0.935 (95% CI, 0.908-0.962).

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217Aβ42Triage

Added October 14, 2026 · DOI:10.1186/s13195-026-02218-x

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The practical message is about test sequencing, not simply which analyte has the highest AUC. A p-tau217-first pathway followed by the p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio only for intermediate results reduced unresolved cases while avoiding universal ratio testing. External validation and prospective decision-impact testing are still needed.

Study design

Retrospective analysis of 562 consecutive memory-clinic patients assessed from October 2023 through April 2026. Core 1 amyloid status used CSF biomarkers and/or amyloid PET. The study compared p-tau217 alone, universal upfront p-tau217/Aβ42, and a p-tau217-first reflex-ratio workflow using rule-out and rule-in thresholds selected for at least 95% sensitivity and specificity.

Key quantitative results

  • Core 1 amyloid positivity was 71.2% (400/562); p-tau217 AUC was 0.935 (95% CI, 0.908-0.962).
  • The p-tau217 two-threshold approach left 17.8% intermediate, with 94.1% accuracy in the decision zones.
  • Universal upfront p-tau217/Aβ42 improved AUC to 0.946 (p=0.011) but reduced indeterminacy only to 17.1%.
  • The sequential workflow reduced indeterminacy to 12.3%, with sensitivity 0.937, specificity 0.935, PPV 0.973, NPV 0.855, and 56 fewer confirmatory CSF or amyloid-PET tests per 1,000 patients.

What changed

The study tested where a plasma ratio adds operational value and found that targeted reflex use in the p-tau217 gray zone was more efficient than universal upfront ratio testing.

Strength of evidence

Moderate implementation evidence from a consecutive real-world cohort with internal temporal validation and a 15-percentage-point prevalence shift. It remains retrospective, single-center, and internally thresholded.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

A reflex-ratio workflow may reduce unresolved plasma results and prioritize which patients need CSF or amyloid PET, but the numerical cutoffs should not be transferred to another population or platform without validation.

Field medical relevance

Useful for discussions about gray-zone management, reflex algorithms, why a small AUC gain may not translate into a large workflow gain, and the distinction between fewer confirmatory tests and proven patient benefit.

Quanterix or platform relevance

This is directly relevant to automated-platform positioning: the ratio added the most value as a reflex test for the p-tau217 intermediate zone rather than as an upfront replacement for every patient. The cutoffs remain cohort- and platform-specific.

Access or reimbursement relevance

The modeled pathway could reduce CSF or amyloid-PET use, but the study did not measure actual costs, reimbursement, access, or realized downstream utilization.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does the ratio replace p-tau217 as the first test?
Not in this study. Its largest operational benefit came when used only after an intermediate p-tau217 result.
Can these cutoffs be used in another laboratory?
No. They were selected and validated internally in one specialty-clinic cohort on the Lumipulse G600II.
Did the workflow improve patient outcomes?
No. It modeled diagnostic classification and confirmatory-test use; it did not prospectively test treatment decisions or outcomes.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Retrospective single-center design
  • High specialty-clinic amyloid prevalence
  • Internally selected thresholds
  • CSF and/or PET composite reference
  • No prospective decision-impact or patient-outcome trial
